trial_design_summary: BCIRG-006: HER2-positive early breast cancer randomized to AC followed by docetaxel (AC-T), the same plus trastuzumab (AC-T+H), or docetaxel/carboplatin/trastuzumab (TCH). Both trastuzumab regimens superior to AC-T.

arms.arm_name: AC→T (Doxorubicin and Cyclophosphamide followed by Docetaxel)
arms.evidence: No significant differences in efficacy were found between the two trastuzumab regimens, whereas both were superior to AC-T.

arms.arm_name: AC→TH (Doxorubicin and Cyclophosphamide followed by Docetaxel and Trastuzumab)
arms.evidence: The addition of 1 year of adjuvant trastuzumab significantly improved disease-free and overall survival.
We wanted to evaluate the efficacy and safety of a new nonanthracycline regimen with trastuzumab.

trial_design_summary: FIRM-ACT: advanced adrenocortical carcinoma randomized to mitotane plus EDP (etoposide, doxorubicin, cisplatin) versus mitotane plus streptozocin. EDP-mitotane had higher response and longer PFS.

arms.evidence: Patients in the EDP-mitotane group had a significantly higher response rate than those in the streptozocin-mitotane group.

arms.arm_name: Arm A (EDP/M: Etoposide, Doxorubicin, Cisplatin, Mitotane)
arms.evidence: Rates of response and progression-free survival were significantly better with EDP plus mitotane than with streptozocin plus mitotane as first-line therapy.

trial_design_summary: Four-regimen factorial antiemetic trial for delayed nausea (palonosetron vs granisetron; +/- day 2-3 dexamethasone; aprepitant vs prochlorperazine). All arms are active antiemetic regimens compared pairwise with no single designated control arm.

Phase 3 head-to-head comparison of peripheral-blood stem-cell versus bone marrow transplantation from unrelated donors. Direct comparison of two graft sources with no designated standard-of-care or control arm.

Combined TEXT+SOFT analysis comparing exemestane plus ovarian suppression versus tamoxifen plus ovarian suppression in premenopausal HR-positive breast cancer; exemestane+OFS reduced recurrence. Abstract addresses only the OFS-containing arms, not tamoxifen alone.

arms.evidence: exemestane plus ovarian suppression, as compared with tamoxifen plus ovarian suppression, significantly reduced recurrence.

arms.arm_name: TEXT Arm A & B (GnRH analogue + Tamoxifen/Exemestane)
TEXT Arm A (GnRH analogue plus Tamoxifen)
arms.evidence: exemestane plus ovarian suppression, as compared with tamoxifen plus ovarian suppression, significantly reduced recurrence.

arms.arm_name: TEXT Arm B (GnRH analogue plus Exemestane)
arms.evidence: adjuvant treatment with exemestane plus ovarian suppression... significantly reduced recurrence.

trial_design_summary: SOFT: premenopausal HR-positive breast cancer randomized to tamoxifen, tamoxifen plus ovarian suppression, or exemestane plus ovarian suppression. Primary test was whether adding ovarian suppression to tamoxifen improves disease-free survival.

arms.evidence: tested the hypothesis that tamoxifen plus ovarian suppression would improve disease-free survival, as compared with tamoxifen alone.
for women... who remained premenopausal, the addition of ovarian suppression improved disease outcomes.
Further improvement was seen with the use of exemestane plus ovarian suppression.

trial_design_summary: ABCSG-18: double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of adjuvant denosumab 60 mg versus placebo every 6 months in postmenopausal aromatase-inhibitor-treated HR-positive breast cancer. Denosumab delayed time to first clinical fracture.

arms.evidence: randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive either denosumab 60 mg or placebo administered subcutaneously every 6 months.
Adjuvant denosumab 60 mg twice per year reduces the risk of clinical fractures in postmenopausal women with breast cancer.

trial_design_summary: PMID-MISMATCH: arm_names describe radiosurgery +/- whole-brain radiotherapy, but the abstract reports EP2006 (a filgrastim biosimilar) versus reference filgrastim for preventing severe neutropenia in breast cancer. Different drugs and disease setting entirely.

TAILORx 21-gene assay validation. This abstract reports only the recurrence-score 0-10 cohort assigned to endocrine therapy alone without chemotherapy; it is a single observational arm with no chemotherapy-comparator results and no designated intervention/control roles.

EURAMOS-1 poor-responder randomization: high-grade osteosarcoma with poor preoperative response randomized to postoperative MAP versus MAP plus ifosfamide/etoposide (MAPIE). MAPIE added toxicity without improving event-free survival; MAP defines standard of care. The MAP-plus-interferon (good-responder) arm is not addressed here.

arms.evidence: either postoperative cisplatin, doxorubicin, and methotrexate (MAP) or MAP plus ifosfamide and etoposide (MAPIE)... results define standard of care.
do not support the addition of ifosfamide and etoposide to postoperative chemotherapy... associated with increased toxicity.

trial_design_summary: SWOG S0518: phase 3 head-to-head comparison of depot octreotide plus interferon alfa-2b versus depot octreotide plus bevacizumab in advanced carcinoid/NETs. Symmetric comparison with similar antitumor activity and no designated standard-of-care or control arm.

GOG-0213 bevacizumab objective: platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer randomized to standard paclitaxel-carboplatin chemotherapy versus the same plus bevacizumab. Adding bevacizumab improved median overall survival. The secondary cytoreductive-surgery objective is ongoing and not reported here.

arms.evidence: randomly assigned (1:1) to standard chemotherapy (six 3-weekly cycles of paclitaxel and carboplatin) or the same chemotherapy regimen plus bevacizumab.
The addition of bevacizumab to standard chemotherapy, followed by maintenance therapy until progression, improved the median overall survival.

trial_design_summary: CALGB/SWOG 80405: KRAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer, first-line FOLFOX/FOLFIRI randomized to cetuximab versus bevacizumab. Pure head-to-head of two biologics with no significant survival difference and no designated standard-of-care or control arm.

Placebo-controlled randomized trial of perioperative gabapentin versus active placebo (lorazepam) in a mixed surgical cohort, assessing time to pain resolution and opioid cessation. Only two randomized arms are described; no observational arm is reported.

arms.evidence: Gabapentin... or active placebo (lorazepam, 0.5 mg) preoperatively followed by inactive placebo postoperatively.
To determine the effect of perioperative gabapentin on remote postoperative time to pain resolution and opioid cessation.

trial_design_summary: PMID-MISMATCH: arm_names describe VMP versus daratumumab-VMP (multiple myeloma), but the abstract is a phase 1 dose-escalation study of momelotinib plus gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel in metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma. Different drugs and disease entirely.

ARM-STRUCTURE-MISMATCH: drug matches (GS-1101 = idelalisib), but arm_names describe standard-dose versus high-dose GS-1101, whereas the abstract reports idelalisib (single 150 mg dose) plus rituximab versus placebo plus rituximab in relapsed CLL. The abstract does not describe any dose-level comparison arms.
